newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian union says labour talks unsuccessful.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian union says labour talks unsuccessful.

text.p: Slovenia's largest trade union, the Association of Free Trade Unions (ZZZS), said on Monday talks with employers concerning labour benefits have been unsuccessful so far.
"It will be very hard to reach an agreement by the end of May as planned earlier. Our standpoints are still too far apart," the secretary of the union Rajko Lesjak told Reuters.
Slovenian unions, the Chamber of Economy and the Association of Employers started talks in January on changes to the collective agreement that determines work benefits.
The new agreement should replace the current one introduced in 1990, renewed in 1993 and expiring at the end of May.
Last year, employers pushed for a reduction of daily allowances, holiday and sick pay, redundancy payments and strike compensation in financially-troubled companies.
"We cannot agree to a substantial reduction of practically all benefits as companies want to reduce their expenses solely on account of lower work payments," Lesjak said.
He said the ZZZS would push for the current agreement to be prolonged until the end of this year if there is no major turnaround in the negotiations in the next couple of weeks.
Employers said lower work payments were a precondition for improved international competitiveness of Slovenia's economy.

In January, average gross pay in Slovenia reached 138,586 tolars ($882), which was 1.6 percent lower than in December 1996 but 15.8 percent higher than in January last year. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
